sections.title: What are Determiners?
sections.source_content: Words that fix the nouns that follow them are called Determiners.
sections.bengali_explanation: যে শব্দগুলি পরবর্তী noun-কে নির্দিষ্ট বা সীমাবদ্ধ করে, সেগুলিকে Determiner বলে।
examples: Which book do you want?
Some boys are playing.
Many girls were singing.
This house is mine.
Give me a pen.
The pen is red.
Give me an umbrella.
Every boy will get a prize.
All men are mortal.
Neither of the boys went there.

sections.title: Classes of Determiners
sections.source_content: Classes: (a) Articles a/an/the (b) Interrogative which/what/whose (c) Possessive my/your/his/her/our/their/its (d) Demonstrative this/that/these/those (e) Distributive each/every/both/neither/either (f) Quantity and Number one/two/some/many/any/few/little/several/much/all/enough etc.
sections.bengali_explanation: Determiners-এর শ্রেণী: Articles, Interrogative, Possessive, Demonstrative, Distributive, Quantity/Number.।

sections.title: Articles
sections.source_content: A, An and The are called Articles. Formerly a separate part of speech; now classed as Adjectives.
sections.bengali_explanation: A, An এবং The-কে Article বলে। আগে আলাদা part of speech, এখন Adjective.।

sections.title: Indefinite Articles A / An
sections.source_content: A and An are Indefinite Articles. They do not point out any particular person or thing. Used only before singular countable nouns. a book = any book; a girl = any girl.
sections.bengali_explanation: A এবং An Indefinite Article। নির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তি/বস্তু নয়। শুধু singular countable noun-এর আগে।

sections.title: Definite Article The
sections.source_content: The is the Definite Article. It points to some particular person or thing. Used before singular or plural, countable or uncountable nouns.
sections.bengali_explanation: The Definite Article। নির্দিষ্ট ব্যক্তি/বস্তু নির্দেশ করে।

sections.title: Common Noun Rule
sections.source_content: Singular common noun generally needs an article. Plural does not need the unless particularised. Boys love games. The boys are playing.
sections.bengali_explanation: Singular common noun-এ article লাগে। Plural-এ particularize না করলে the লাগে না।

sections.title: Rules for A
sections.source_content: A before consonant sound (a boy, a B.A.), before yu sound (a university, a European, a useful thing), before one sound (a one-rupee note). Choice is based on SOUND, not spelling.
sections.bengali_explanation: A: consonant sound, yu sound, one sound-এর আগে। উচ্চারণ দেখে সিদ্ধান্ত নিতে হয়।
examples: a boy, a word, a B.A.
a university, a European, a useful thing
a one-rupee note, a one-eyed person

sections.title: Rules for An
sections.source_content: An before vowel sound (an eye, an ox, an umbrella) and before consonant with vowel sound (an M.A., an heir, an honest boy, an hour). Modern usage: a historical, a humble when h is pronounced.
sections.bengali_explanation: An: vowel sound এবং vowel-sound consonant (hour, honest, M.A.)-এর আগে।
examples: an eye, an idiot, an ox, an umbrella
an M.A., an heir, an honest boy, an hour

sections.title: Other Uses of A and An
sections.source_content: Generalizing (A son should obey his father). As preposition (one kilo a rupee). A certain (A Mr Bose). Fixed phrases (in a hurry, have a cold). a few / a little (= some) vs few / little (= not many/much). Exclamatory (What a thing to say!).
sections.bengali_explanation: সাধারণীকরণ, preposition, a certain, fixed phrase, a few/a little, exclamatory.।

sections.title: Rules for The
sections.source_content: The is used before: rivers/seas (the Ganga, the Black Sea); mountain ranges (the Himalayas) but NOT single peaks (Everest); groups of islands (the Andamans); ships/newspapers/holy books (the Titanic, the Bible); public buildings (the Tajmahal); events (the French Revolution); trains (the Rajdhani Express); deserts (the Sahara); institutions with non-personal names; countries that are unions/plural (the U.K., the U.S.A.); generalising class (The dog is faithful); unique things (the sun, the earth); directions as nouns (the east); superlatives (the best); nationalities as people (The English); adjectives as class (the rich, the blind); possessive body parts (on the head); ordinals (George the Fifth); professions (the Bar); musical instruments when playing (the violin); family names (the Browns); unit of measurement (by the dozen).
sections.bengali_explanation: The: নদী, সাগর, পর্বতমালা, জাহাজ, পত্রিকা, ধর্মগ্রন্থ, মরুভূমি, superlative, জাতি, the rich, on the head, the violin, by the dozen ইত্যাদি।

sections.title: Omission of Articles
sections.source_content: No article: proper/material/abstract nouns in general sense; plural common nouns; after kind/sort of; man=mankind; father/mother/baby in family sense; cook/nurse = our cook; idioms (by boat, at night); school/hospital for purpose (go to school / go to hospital); parks/streets with proper names (Curzon Park); meals as routine; seasons; title + personal name (President Kennedy); factitive complements (elected captain). Contrast: go to school (learn) vs go to the school (visit building).
sections.bengali_explanation: Article বাদ: proper/abstract/material, plural, man=mankind, school/hospital purpose অর্থে, meal, season, title+name.। go to school vs go to the school.।

sections.title: Repetition of the Article
sections.source_content: Same person/thing: article only once. The Secretary and Treasurer has done this. Different persons: repeat article. The Secretary and the Treasurer have done this. Same with adjectives: a brown and white cat (one) vs a brown and a white cat (two).
sections.bengali_explanation: একই ব্যক্তি/বস্তু = article একবার। আলাদা = প্রত্যেকের আগে article.।
examples: The Secretary and Treasurer has done this. (same)
The Secretary and the Treasurer have done this. (two)
a brown and white cat (one)
a brown and a white cat (two)

sections.title: Key Contrasts for Exams
examples: a university vs an umbrella
a European vs an honest man
a one-rupee note vs an hour
The Ganga vs Everest
The English (people) vs English (language)
go to school vs go to the school
a few vs few
a little vs little
The Secretary and Treasurer vs The Secretary and the Treasurer

sections.title: Exercise 11 Practice Areas
sections.description: a/an before words; fill blanks; passages; insert articles; correct sentences.
